notes: Batch 27 CLOSED 2026-09-28. Full narrative in docs/journey-runs/BATCH_27_RESULTS.md. The user required a mid-batch reconciliation pass before continuing past V-020, correcting four items that had been under-verified: (1) V-010 redone as the full canonical scenario (a live request bound to published version A, a materially edited and published version B that removed the exact node in question, confirming the request stayed bound to A, its next action succeeded normally, and audit/recovery were intact), not merely 'published versions are immutable'. (2) V-016 reclassified EXPECTED BEHAVIOR (not plain PASS): the canonical's two-different-draft-versions premise cannot occur at all, blocked by the genuine, stronger uq_workflow_version_one_draft structural invariant; Journey Discovery then found L-015 as existing near-duplicate coverage and the missing publish-specific variant was executed as an EXPAND_EXISTING_JOURNEY addition to L-015 rather than a new duplicate journey. (3) V-013's cross-reference to V-001 was checked assertion-by-assertion; five of six required assertions were already proven, and the one genuine gap (recovery after reload) was executed as the only missing piece. (4) V-019's 'UI-scoping open question' was resolved via formal Journey Discovery rather than left flagged: source investigation found two entirely separate routes (submitter-facing /customers/.../change-requests/[id] with no approve controls by design, versus the real reviewer route /reviews/change-requests/[id]), confirmed via browser as the correct eligible-reviewer route rendering full Approve/Send Back/Reject controls; disposition ALREADY_COVERED (a testing-methodology artifact, not a product gap). After reconciliation, V-020 through V-029 were executed. V-024 and V-025 (role revoke and account disable while a session/page was already live) were tested with a real browser: a fixture Customer Change request was reattached to a Finance-team node so nexus-test-finance-b had a genuine rendered Approve button, then the Checker role was revoked (V-024) and separately the account was disabled (V-025) without reloading the page; both produced real, distinct Server Action denials captured directly from the network response body ('You do not have permission to approve customer for this customer.' and 'Your Nexus account is no longer active.' respectively), zero mutation confirmed in both cases, both restored afterward. V-026 and V-027 reused one request across the Legal then Leadership nodes of a 2-member-team graph: removing one of two members (V-026) let the remaining member approve normally with no disruption; removing the last two (zero active members, V-027) produced a real, confirmed WORKFLOW_TEAM_REQUIRED stuck state that recovered cleanly once membership was restored. V-027 was reclassified from PASS to PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED after the user pointed out the canonical journey explicitly calls this stuck state 'a real, confirmed unhandled gap' worth product attention, not merely a test to pass; no rerun was needed, the existing execution evidence (genuine stuck state, no silent transition, clean recovery) already established the mechanism. This gap is not new: it already has a formally closed decision from Batch 6 (O-018, disposition C/USER PRODUCT DECISION REQUIRED at the time, later decided as 'warn but allow' and genuinely implemented via checkTeamRemovalImpactAction plus an Operations Queue 'no eligible approver' banner in the real team-removal UI). V-027's raw RPC-based execution sits underneath that UI warning layer, so it reconfirms the same well-established mechanism (previously proven independently in A-027, C-025, E-028, J-011, and O-018 itself) rather than reopening or duplicating O-018's already-closed decision. V-028 executed the full canonical multi-step scenario (one real user approved node 3 as a Legal team member, was added to the Leadership team before the request reached node 4, then successfully approved node 4 too) and root-caused it via direct source read of approve_customer_change_request: the function's only identity check compares the actor to created_by (the original submitter) and never checks this request's own workflow_node_transitions history for prior approvers, so the same person can legitimately decide two sequential levels. Classified PRODUCT_GAP_CONFIRMED per the canonical's own anticipation of this exact finding, with a new open Product Decision (add a cross-node distinct-approver control, or accept current behavior since team membership is itself admin-governed). V-020 and V-029 both classified PARTIAL/TOOLING_LIMITATION, same class as Batch 26's AB-030/036/037 (no request-pausing proxy or server-side failpoint available in this environment to land a permission change inside a true microsecond in-flight window); logged individually to the Morning Residual Queue, not blocking closure. Cumulative open Product Decisions across the run: 3 (AB-020's reference_master maker-checker gap, AB-043/AB-039's loser-experience-consistency question, and V-028's cross-node distinct-approver question), none double-counted. Cumulative confirmed product gaps across the run: 4 (AB-020, AB-039, V-027, V-028); V-027 does not add a fourth open decision since its decision (O-018) was already closed in Batch 6. No new defects found or fixed this batch.
